standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: lemma-algebraically-closed (factorization over an algebraic closure), lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure (extension of embeddings), lemma-characterize-normal (normality via equal images of embeddings)
core_obligations: Existence and minimality: in an algebraic closure write P = c (x - beta_1) ... (x - beta_n) and set E = F(beta_1, ..., beta_n); any extension over which P splits completely contains all beta_i, hence contains E, so E is minimal

Normality and uniqueness: for another minimal E' = F(alpha_1, ..., alpha_n), any F-embedding sigma of E' into the algebraic closure sends each alpha_i to some beta_tau(i) (both are the full root sets of P in the closure), so sigma(E') = E; by lemma-characterize-normal E' is normal over F, and sigma restricts to an F-isomorphism E' -> E
proof_roadmap: Build E inside an algebraic closure and prove minimality by generation
Prove normality and uniqueness through the embedding permutation argument
